memos.scout:
Case for buying Origin now:

The curve looks organic. Bundle share is 5.3% and top-3 holders hold 6.8%, with no airdrop dump. The completer share of 27% suggests a broad set of buyers filled the bonding curve rather than one operator. Over the last 15 minutes it drew 160 buyers and 55.5 SOL of buying against 49.8 SOL of selling, a net inflow of 5.7 SOL, and it is up 10.6% over 30 minutes. It has pulled back only 7.6% from its 30-minute high, which is a shallow dip for a coin still drawing new buyers.

Weaknesses: the first two minutes after graduation showed a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.92 and a launch bot was present, and the pool is thin at 89.6 SOL. Round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% eat into any short-term gain. Treat this as a modest-conviction scout, not a strong buy.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution into a thin pool. Over the last 15 minutes, sell SOL (49.77) nearly matched buy SOL (55.46), leaving net flow of only +5.69 SOL, and sellers (112) are most of the buyer count (160). The first two minutes after graduation showed a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.92 and a launch bot, so early participants were already flipping. The completer holds 27.1% of the curve, a large position that can be sold into any bounce, and the 1.1% of the pool that is the 89.6 SOL depth means a $20 round trip faces 1.4-5.1% fees and impact before any move. A 7.6% drawdown from the 30-minute high is already underway. The bundle share (5.3%) and top-3 share (6.8%) look clean, but the completer's stake matters more. With fees eating small moves and sellers dominating, I'd skip.
